identifying_markers: Distinct spectacle mark on dorsal hood
first_aid: Immobilize the bitten limb immediately below heart level.
Apply broad pressure bandage over the bite area (do not block arterial pulse).
Do NOT cut, suck, incise, or apply electric shock.
Keep patient calm to slow systemic lymphatic absorption.
Rush immediately to the nearest hospital equipped with Polyvalent Anti-Venom Serum (AVS).
notes: Responsible for highest number of neurotoxic envenomations in India. Part of the 'Big Four'.

identifying_markers: Flat triangular head distinct from neck
Deep brown chain-like circular spots in 3 longitudinal rows
symptoms: Spontaneous bleeding from gums, bite wounds
first_aid: Keep the affected limb completely still and splinted.
Do NOT apply a tight arterial tourniquet (causes localized gangrene).
Remove tight jewelry, rings, or tight clothing immediately.
Administer whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) on hospital arrival.
Immediate transport to emergency trauma center with AVS and dialysis standby.
notes: Causes profound coagulopathy and acute renal failure. Part of the 'Big Four'.

identifying_markers: Glossy steel-black or dark bluish-brown body
Distinct narrow paired white cross-bands along spine
Enlarged hexagonal vertebral scales down middle of back
symptoms: Painless nocturnal bite (often mistaken for insect bite)
first_aid: Immediate emergency medical dispatch even if bite mark is painless or invisible.
Prepare for emergency assisted mechanical ventilation.
Do NOT delay hospital transit for non-symptom observation.
Polyvalent AVS administration is urgently required.
notes: 15x more toxic than Cobra venom. Envenomation often occurs while victims sleep on the floor.

region: Dry semi-arid regions, rocks, red soil, scrub forests
identifying_markers: White cruciform or bird-foot mark on crown of head
Serrated flank scales that produce raspy sawing noise
first_aid: Immobilize limb.
Avoid NSAIDs / Aspirin (worsens hemorrhage).
Expedited evacuation to hospital with AVS.
notes: Smallest of the Big Four venomous snakes, but responsible for high morbidity in arid zones.

identifying_markers: Large yellowish-brown body with prominent black net-like markings on tail
symptoms: No systemic neurotoxic or hemotoxic symptoms
first_aid: Wash wound thoroughly with clean water and antiseptic soap.
Apply mild antiseptic and clean dry dressing.
Check Tetanus Toxoid (TT) vaccination status.
Reassure victim against panic.
notes: Often confused with Spectacled Cobra due to size and coloration, but completely harmless and beneficial rodent predator.
